headline_marked: State Minister [[Ishraque Hossain brandishes firearm]] during anti-drug drive
headline: State Minister Ishraque Hossain brandishes firearm during anti-drug drive
summary: Videos showing the Minister for Liberation War Affairs carrying a gun while chasing suspects in Gandaria have sparked widespread public outrage.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain was seen carrying a firearm while conducting an "anti-drug operation" in Gandaria, Dhaka.
The minister uploaded videos of the raid to his Facebook page, showing him and his security guards chasing suspects and demolishing drug dens near the railway line.
In the videos, Ishraque and several guards were carrying firearms, with one guard seen pointing a gun at people and kicking an individual.
The Gandaria Police Station OC confirmed that six people were detained during the operation, though he noted that while he didn't see the weapon personally, he saw it in the video.
Ishraque told Prothom Alo that the firearm is licensed and was acquired after December 12, 2025, which is why it wasn't in his election nomination papers.
The minister defended his actions, claiming he carried the weapon because police lack manpower and vehicles, and drug traders in the area often fire at law enforcers.
Former IGP Baharul Alam warned that displaying firearms in a way that causes fear or discomfort is prohibited under the Firearms Licence, Renewal and Use Policy 2025.
The policy also prohibits licensed holders from being employed as armed guards to protect others, which could lead to the immediate revocation of of the license.
caption:
A State Minister caught on video brandishing a firearm during a drug raid. Is this law enforcement or taking the law into one's own hands?

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain was seen carrying a firearm while conducting an "anti-drug operation" in Gandaria, Dhaka.

The minister uploaded videos of the raid to his Facebook page, showing him and his security guards chasing suspects and demolishing drug dens near the railway line.

In the videos, Ishraque and several guards were carrying firearms, with one guard seen pointing a gun at people and kicking an individual.

The Gandaria Police Station OC confirmed that six people were detained during the operation, though he noted that while he didn't see the weapon personally, he saw it in the video.

Ishraque told Prothom Alo that the firearm is licensed and was acquired after December 12, 2025, which is why it wasn't in his election nomination papers.

The minister defended his actions, claiming he carried the weapon because police lack manpower and vehicles, and drug traders in the area often fire at law enforcers.

Former IGP Baharul Alam warned that displaying firearms in a way that causes fear or discomfort is prohibited under the Firearms Licence, Renewal and Use Policy 2025.

The policy also prohibits licensed holders from being employed as armed guards to protect others, which could lead to the immediate revocation of of the license.

topic: pm stresses national interest and sovereignty
headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman: [[National interest and sovereignty]] to define Bangladesh's future
headline: PM Tarique Rahman: National interest and sovereignty to define Bangladesh's future
summary: The Prime Minister pledged to protect national interests and self-respect while strengthening global cooperation based on mutual respect and equality.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that protecting national interests, sovereignty, and self-respect will be the core commitments of Bangladesh’s future during a ceremony at Savar Cantonment on Sunday.
The event was held to present National Standards (national flags) to seven battalions and regiments of the Bangladesh Army in recognition of their professional achievements.
The PM emphasized that the National Standard is a symbol of a unit's history, discipline, and commitment to the country, urging soldiers to uphold the honor of the flag as a sacred duty.

He noted that modern armed forces rely not only on weapons but on discipline, competence, leadership, ethics, and public trust, adding that the government is working to make the military more technology-driven and professional.

Tarique Rahman highlighted the changing nature of warfare, citing the importance of cyberspace, drones, AI, and electronic warfare in national security, and stated that efforts are underway to ensure defense preparedness keeps pace.
The government is prioritizing the establishment of a domestic defense industry to manufacture essential weapons and ammunition in Bangladesh, alongside modernizing the army in all areas.
Regarding personnel welfare, the PM mentioned that salaries and allowances for armed forces members have been increased by 100% to 138% under the national pay scale.
He also mentioned that the implementation of the 'One Rank, One Pension' system is being processed to further improve the living standards of army personnel.
